findings.body: *No test coverage for `src/config.ts`'s new validation logic.** `config.check()` is new: it collects multiple problems instead of throwing on the first (previously only `PORT` was validated via immediate `throw`), and it adds a brand-new `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` check that didn't exist before. Zero tests exercise either the multi-problem collection or the new field validation — `test/` only covers `health.ts` via `server.ts`. Worth a small `test/config.test.ts` covering: valid config → `[]`, invalid `PORT` → problem, invalid `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` → problem, both invalid → both problems.

findings.body: **`pkg/factory/runner.go:66`** — `ResolvePosters` lives inside `pkg/factory/` and is a non-`Create*` function containing a conditional (`if cfg.SkipPost`), which the rule's own scope text (any file under `pkg/factory/`, not just `factory.go`) reads as a hit. *(rule: `go-factory/no-impl-in-factory-pkg`)* — **disputed**: `go-architecture-assistant` argues this is not a violation, citing the pre-existing `ResolveBotLogin` (`pkg/factory/botlogin.go`) as established precedent for a `Resolve*`-prefixed, same-package helper that selects between wiring options without doing I/O itself — exactly the precedent the dark-factory prompt cited when specifying this placement. Since the precedent predates this PR and was never previously flagged, this reads more as a rule-text/practice gap than a regression introduced here. Worth a maintainer call on whether to tighten the rule's `applies_when` or move the helper into `main.go`'s `Run`.

**`pkg/skip_post_boundary_test.go`** — the 4-case nil-interface contract test drives coverage through full `reviewStep.Run`/`postAndRoute` execution (2 mocks, markdown fixtures) to prove a property — "is this a genuine nil interface, not a boxed nil pointer" — that a direct `poster == nil` comparison in `pkg/factory/runner_test.go` would prove more cheaply at the unit level. *(rule: `test-pyramid/push-down-when-unsure`)* Note: this integration-style approach was a deliberate, well-documented choice across the three dark-factory prompts that built this file (specifically to exercise the real production guards, not just the interface property in isolation) — flagging as optional, not a defect.
